final_message:
I implemented `expand_field` and `parse_cron` in `cronfields/fields.py` following the README. All 3 tests pass.

I also spot-checked the README examples (`*/20` → `[0, 20, 40]`, `2,10-12,11` → `[2, 10, 11, 12]`, weekday `5-7` → `[0, 5, 6]`) and a set of invalid inputs (empty items, `5/2`, signs, decimals, unknown names, `*/0`, reversed ranges, out-of-range values, doubled `/` or `-`). All of the invalid inputs raise `ValueError`.

Design choices:
- Values are collected into a set and returned sorted, so overlapping items produce each value once.
- Name lookup is case-insensitive and applies wherever a number is accepted.
- The weekday `7` → `0` mapping happens in `parse_cron`, after expansion, so `0,7` yields `[0]`.
- `parse_cron` splits on any whitespace run and requires exactly five fields.

 """Expansion of cron time fields."""
 
+import re
 from collections.abc import Mapping
 
 MONTHS = {name: number for number, name in enumerate("JAN FEB MAR APR MAY JUN JUL AUG SEP OCT NOV DEC".split(), 1)}
 WEEKDAYS = {name: number for number, name in enumerate("SUN MON TUE WED THU FRI SAT".split())}
 
+_DIGITS = re.compile(r"[0-9]+")
+
+
+def _number(token: str, lo: int, hi: int, names: Mapping[str, int] | None) -> int:
+    """Parse a single value token (a name or plain decimal digits) and check it lies within lo..hi."""
+    if names is not None and token.upper() in names:
+        return names[token.upper()]
+    if not _DIGITS.fullmatch(token):
+        raise ValueError(f"invalid value: {token!r}")
+    value = int(token)
+    if not lo <= value <= hi:
+        raise ValueError(f"value {value} out of range {lo}-{hi}")
+    return value
